items.title: Flipping a House Isn’t Paying Like It Used To. Is Renting the Better Bet?
items.summary:
The typical home flip generated just $60,526 in gross profit in the second quarter of 2026, down from $71,000 a year earlier, according to new data—before accounting for renovation costs or other expenses.

It's a shrinking cushion for investors who have long relied on a simple formula to fuel their business: Buy low , apply elbow grase, and sell high. But with elevated borrowing costs and renovation expenses eating into margins, there's much less room than there used to be for anything to go wrong.

The report, from real estate data analytics company ATTOM , found that flipping returns have been declining for two years, with the typical gross return falling to 21.5%, from 27.6% a year earlier.

"Flippers are still making money in most markets, but the typical return continues to narrow," Rob Barber , CEO of ATTOM, said via press release. "The second-quarter numbers continue the general downward trend in profit margins and gross profits we have seen over the past two years."

So, why not skip the resale altogether and rent out the property instead?

After all, the promise of passive income—collecting rent every month while building equity—helped fuel a wave of small investors buying up homes earlier this decade when borrowing costs were low and rents were on a meteoric rise.

But the economics have changed for landlords, too.

Potential rental yields declined in more than half of U.S. counties with comparable data between 2025 and 2026, according to separate ATTOM research . That's to say nothing of the work involved in managing a rental property, which, as Realtor.com®…
items.t: Flipping a House Isn’t Paying Like It Used To. Is Renting the Better Bet?

items.title: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul Signs New Private Listings Bill
items.summary:
New York has signed a new private listings bill, which means that properties will be required to be visible to the public as they hit the market unless the seller signs an informed opt-out consent.

Late last week, Gov. Kathy Hochul signed the Fair and Transparent Real Estate Listing Act . The language of the bill requires that real estate listings be marketed in "at least one other publication, platform or website that does not require payment" or for the consumer to work with the brokerage for access.

This follows a quick path through the state's Legislature, which approved the act in a noncontroversial vote in June. The New York State Association of Realtors® strongly supports the bill.

This becomes the latest crackdown on private listings, where a real estate agent markets a property to a limited list of buyers before making it public.

Fair housing advocates say private listings raise discrimination concerns. One study from Bright MLS found private listings take longer to sell and don't guarantee more money.

The listing must be accessible to the general public, "without limitation to a particular brokerage, franchise or select group of licenses." Also, there can't be restrictions on some or all of the details in the listing, according to the language of the bill.

The bill doesn't require a seller or lister to hold open houses or public showings if it violates any state or federal laws related to health and safety. And sellers can opt out, by signing a form that explicitly warns them that the listing will have limited visibility and possible impact on the price…
items.t: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul Signs New Private Listings Bill

items.title: Buying a Home Soon? This Overlooked Open Enrollment Perk Could Save You Thousands in Legal Fees
items.summary:
Buying a home comes with enough expenses already. Between inspections , title insurance , closing costs, and a stack of paperwork that seems to grow every day, it's easy to lose track of what you're paying for.

But what if your employer could help cover some of the legal bills?

It's a possibility many homebuyers may overlook during open enrollment, when employees are typically comparing health insurance premiums and retirement benefits rather than thinking about hiring a lawyer.

Employer-sponsored legal plans, offered through companies such as LegalShield , MetLife and ARAG , can provide access to attorneys for a modest monthly fee.

A real estate attorney can review a purchase agreement, make sure inspection and financing contingencies actually protect the buyer, check the deed and title, examine mortgage documents, and represent a buyer at closing. Depending on the plan, some or all of that may be covered.

Jago Gavin , a LegalShield representative who works with employer groups, tells Realtor.com® that the real value is having someone to consult before signing something you might not fully understand.

"The law is not logical; it's legal," Gavin says.

That's relevant when buying a house , where an unfamiliar contract provision can have expensive consequences.

Gavin recalls a LegalShield member whose attorney spotted a potentially unfavorable mediation clause in real estate paperwork and recommended changing it before the buyer signed.

The potential savings can run from hundreds to thousands of dollars. But there's a catch: Not all legal plans offer the same…
items.t: Buying a Home Soon? This Overlooked Open Enrollment Perk Could Save You Thousands in Legal Fees

items.title: Why an Uninsulated Garage Can Wreak Havoc on Your Home This Winter
items.summary:
An uninsulated garage might seem like no big deal, but come the winter months, it can do more harm than good. 

In fact, when a garage lacks proper insulation during the colder months, frozen pipes, heat loss, and damaged items are bound to arise. 

Fortunately, insulation solutions and preventive measures can help you avoid these issues while protecting your garage, your car, and your home . 

Risks of uninsulated garages during the winter 

An uninsulated garage in the winter months can cause a chain reaction of issues to the home itself. One of the most common risks is frozen pipes. 

“When the plumbing or water lines located in the garage get exposed to below-freezing temps, they may freeze and cause water damage,” explains Chris Boyle , in-house repair tech at Parts Town Home and Fix.com in Nova Scotia . 

Additionally, improperly insulated garages can prompt heat loss throughout the entire home. 

“Many poorly insulated garages share foundations with homes. As a result, cold air may circulate through the living spaces and force families to turn up their heating systems,” says Boyle.

Not only does this put a strain on HVAC systems, it can also drive up monthly heating bills. 

Plus, poor insulation may damage items stored in the garage, particularly car batteries, which can lose charge or fail completely. 

Winterizing your garage can save you more money than you might imagine. (Getty Images) 

How to tell if your garage is insulated 

So, how do you know for sure whether your garage is insulated?

On a cold day, compare the temperature inside your garage to the…
items.t: Why an Uninsulated Garage Can Wreak Havoc on Your Home This Winter

items.title: New Homes Are Now $40K Cheaper Than Existing Homes
items.summary:
New-construction homes are less expensive than existing ones, and the difference has never been larger, the National Association of Home Builders has found.

Last month's NAHB/Wells Fargo Cost of Housing Index found the median new-home price is $393,300, compared to a median-priced existing home, which comes to $432,900 in the third quarter of 2026. That's the largest difference between new- and existing-home prices in the history of NAHB's tracking, Chairman Bill Owens said.

Builders, struggling to find buyers, are digging deeper to offer incentives on new homes. The  National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index  plunged to a 14-year low last week. Many of the nation's major homebuilders have reported large year-over-year declines in revenue. But housing starts continue apace , showing some hope for the market long term.

“Builders are working with buyers to make new homes more affordable and appealing in a tough market, yet the latest CHI data show housing costs still overburden families,” NAHB Chief Economist Robert Dietz said in a statement.

A typical family would have to pay 36% of their income for a median-priced existing home. They'd need 33% of their income for a new home, a drop of 1% from the second quarter. And that accounts for a $17,000 drop in the median new-home price in the second quarter, when it was $434,900, NAHB found.

“As builders contend with rising construction costs, tighter lending standards and persistent labor shortages, policymakers should remove regulatory obstacles, enact permitting reform and create a stronger…
items.t: New Homes Are Now $40K Cheaper Than Existing Homes

items.title: Young Adults Living With Parents Surge Fastest in America’s Once-Affordable Regions
items.summary:
Young adults living with their parents have become a familiar symbol of America's housing affordability crisis . But the geography of that living arrangement is changing, according to new research.

A record 25.2 million Americans aged 18 to 34 lived with their parents in 2025, or roughly 1 in 3 young adults. Nationally, that share barely budged between the pooled 2020–22 and 2023–25 periods, according to The Geography of the Crowded Nest , a new report from Realtor.com® .

Beneath that apparent stability, however, the South and Midwest—long considered the nation's affordability havens—recorded the largest year-over-year increases in 2025, with the share living at home rising 1.4 percentage points to 32.3% and 31.7%, respectively.

Meanwhile, in the notoriously expensive Northeast—where living with parents has historically been most common—the rate fell 2.3 percentage points to 36.9%, its lowest level since 2010.

It pushes back against conventional logic that cheaper housing markets offer young adults an easier path to independence.

"This is not a coastal problem that has stayed coastal; it has spread to even the more-accessible parts of the country," writes Hannah Jones , senior economist at Realtor.com and author of the report .

Perhaps the clearest illustration comes from two metros that, at first glance, seem worlds apart: San Antonio, TX, and Boston, MA .

One is steeped in cowboy culture; the other, Ivy League academia. In October, the median asking rent in Boston was $2,954, more than double the $1,117 in San Antonio. Yet the share of young adults living with…
items.t: Young Adults Living With Parents Surge Fastest in America’s Once-Affordable Regions

items.title: Asking Mom and Dad for Down Payment Help This Thanksgiving? Here’s How Much To Ask For
items.summary:
Thanksgiving . A time for turkey, football, and the gathering of family. 

It can be a stressful day for many, from the demands of traveling to the obligations of hosting at home . But hopefully, for most, it’s a day to be spent being thankful for having the loved ones gathered around the table. 

And what better time to ask those loved ones for a bit of help to achieve the American dream than on a quintessential American holiday?

Jokes aside, if it’s on your holiday agenda to hit up Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, or even cool Aunt Janet for some money to buy a home next year, there’s a few things you should know before making the trip.

Like how much you’re actually going to need for that dream home. 

A helping hand 

The reality is, young people really do need help with down payments these days—and many are getting it. 

In the past year, 25% of first-time homebuyers used gifts or loans from family and friends to help fund their down payment, according to the National Association of Realtors® 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers .

Furthermore, whether they’re going it alone or with help, all buyers are strapped for the cash for down payments as overall payments are on the decline. 

The typical down payment share dropped for four straight quarters, softening to 12.8% in the first quarter of 2026, down 1.1 percentage points from a year earlier, according to the most recent Realtor.com® down payment report . 

In dollar terms, down payments sank 19% year over year to their lowest point since the third quarter of 2021.

items.t: Asking Mom and Dad for Down Payment Help This Thanksgiving? Here’s How Much To Ask For

items.title: Housing Week Ahead: International Demand, Home Prices, and New-Home Sales
items.summary:
The coming week brings a number of key indicators and new research from the Realtor.com Economics team, despite the holiday schedule for Thanksgiving Day .

On Monday, new research from senior economist Hannah Jones shows that many Americans won't be traveling far to visit their parents for the holiday. That’s because a third of American adults under 35 years old still live in their parents’ home.

On Wednesday, senior economist Jiayi Xu has our third-quarter International Demand report, showing where home shoppers from different countries are looking at U.S. homes. 

Also on Wednesday, coming out early due to the Thanksgiving holiday, senior economist Jake Krimmel will analyze our weekly housing data for clues on the latest housing market trends in real time. 

For economic indicators being released next week, we’ll see the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Index on Tuesday, along with new-home sales and the Freddie Mac mortgage rate on Wednesday.

The Case-Shiller Index is expected to show national home price growth holding near 2% through September, after the national index rose 2.1% year over year through August . Annual gains have climbed since the spring, but slower median sales price growth and softer contract activity this summer suggest the pickup may be running out of steam.

New-home sales are likely to show another weak month in October, after falling 5.3% year over year in September . The existing-home segment saw softer pending home sales and home purchase closings last month as buyers are faced with affordability challenges due to high mortgage rates.…
items.t: Housing Week Ahead: International Demand, Home Prices, and New-Home Sales

items.title: Cost of renting in Britain to rise twice as fast as buying amid shortage of properties
items.summary:
Rents to rise by 14% until at least 2029, Hamptons predicts, as high demand for properties and low supply push up costs for tenants

The cost of renting a home in Britain is expected to rise about twice as fast as that of buying one until at least 2029, according to research, with shrinking supply pushing up the prices paid by tenants.

Rents on newly agreed lets are forecast to grow by 14.2% between 2026 and 2029, compared with house price growth of 7.2%, according to forecasts from estate agent Hamptons.

items.title: President Woodrow Wilson’s Historic Princeton Home Lists for $5.85 Million After a 7-Year Restoration
items.summary:
The home where Woodrow Wilson lived as a professor before becoming president has hit the market in Princeton, NJ for $5.85 million.

The Tudor Revival at 82 Library Place was built in 1896 for Wilson and he lived there with his wife, Ellen, and their three children until 1902, when he became president of Princeton University and moved on campus. 

The home was first listed in May 2025 for $6.5 million. 

“Wilson and his wife had a lot of input in the design and finishes chosen for the home, which included double stained-glass doors from the Sears catalog,” says listing agent Barbara Blackwell of Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty .

The backyard comes with garden-lined patios and a koi pond (Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty) 

The home underwent a seven year top-to-bottom restoration (Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty) 

Inside the new sunroom (Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty) 

The estate is one of only two working homes in the U.S. designed and built by a president, the other being Monticello, according to the listing. 

Blackwell says the house has had 19 owners since the Wilsons, including Princeton University itself, which used the home as faculty housing during the Great Depression.

The current owners spent seven years restoring the property with architect Ron Berlin and Baxter Construction. The award-winning project brought back the original beams and woodwork and re-glassed the leaded windows. It also gave the home a distinct sense of presidential charm, making it easy to imagine Wilson tucked among…
items.t: President Woodrow Wilson’s Historic Princeton Home Lists for $5.85 Million After a 7-Year Restoration

items.title: This Renovated 1949 Santa Monica Home Looks Like a Movie Set—And It Just Hit the Market for $6.9 Million
items.summary:
A five-bedroom modern retreat nestled on a tree-lined street in Santa Monica, CA has just hit the market for $6,898,000.

Built in 1949, the 4,746-square-foot residence was renovated in 2022 and now features a sun-soaked open floor plan with curated finishes, designer lighting, and walls of windows.

“I love all of the light that comes into the home,” said listing agent Shelton Wilder of Christie’s International Real Estate Southern California . “It has beautiful skylights throughout and it’s located on the side of the street that gets so much natural sunlight. It looks like a movie set.”

Living room of renovated estate in Santa Monica, CA (Neuefocus Photography) 

Kitchen and dining area of renovated estate in Santa Monica, CA (Neuefocus Photography) 

Pool of renovated estate in Santa Monica, CA (Neuefocus Photography) 

Designed for grand-scale entertaining and everyday living, the thoughtful layout offers a lavish primary sanctuary separate from a second-story guest wing that could also be used for extended family.

“The primary suite is so private and very luxurious,” Wilder noted. “It was the primary residence for the sellers, who have owned it for five years. I think the next buyer will use it as a primary as well. It was so special for the sellers who have three kids. It could also be someone with older kids who want to stay there while visiting.”

A sleek chef’s kitchen has two refrigerators, double ovens, custom cabinetry, a breakfast bar, and a built-in coffee machine. Glass doors from the dining area open to the private backyard with an outdoor shower and a…
items.t: This Renovated 1949 Santa Monica Home Looks Like a Movie Set—And It Just Hit the Market for $6.9 Million

items.title: Rare 25-Foot-Wide Carnegie Hill Townhouse With a Private Carriage House Lists for $11.95 Million
items.summary:
A 25-foot-wide townhouse with a carriage house has just hit the market for $11.95 million in Manhattan’s Carnegie Hill .

Built in 1899, the five-bedroom residence underwent a “no-expense-spared” reconstruction and features 13 newly renovated rooms, each with individually zoned heating and cooling.

“It is certainly very rare for a listing like this townhouse with a carriage house to come on the market in uptown Manhattan ,” said listing agent Daniella G. Schlisser of Brown Harris Stevens . “I don’t recall ever seeing something like this here.”

Kitchen of Carnegie Hill townhouse in Manhattan, NY (Jon Nissenbaum / @instaniss) 

Den of Carnegie Hill townhouse in Manhattan, NY (Jon Nissenbaum / @instaniss) 

Dining room of Carnegie Hill townhouse in Manhattan, NY (Jon Nissenbaum / @instaniss) 

The 7,700-square-foot interior was entirely gutted and rebuilt with new structural steel, plumbing, electrical, and commercial-grade mechanical systems.

“It has incredible sun and light, which is incredibly unusual for a townhouse,” Schlisser said. “The home is flooded with direct sunlight facing the back and it also gets sun to the north in the front.”

The six-story dwelling features a garden level that leads to a limestone gallery with custom paneling. There is a separately accessed commercial space offering “continued retail or office use” that could also be transformed into additional living space. French doors open to a bluestone-decked garden with a built-in grill.

“There is a phenomenal amount of space and light, and being a 25-foot-wide townhouse is also rare,” she noted.…
items.t: Rare 25-Foot-Wide Carnegie Hill Townhouse With a Private Carriage House Lists for $11.95 Million

items.title: Inside a Secluded Cabin Hidden Right Beneath Big Sur’s Iconic Landmark
items.summary:
A secluded retreat tucked beneath one of California’s most photographed landmarks in Big Sur has come on the market for $3.65 million.

The home at 39320 Coast Road sits in Bixby Canyon and is one of only seven residences behind a private gate.

“Millions recognize Bixby Bridge, yet very few will ever experience the landscape beneath it,” says listing agent Michael Hornig of the Strock Team at eXp Realty .

The entrance of the cabin, which is one of only seven properties in the canyon. (Lost Coast Media) 

The main room and kitchen (Lost Coast Media) 

A cozy living room (Lost Coast Media) 

The canyon also comes with a literary history: In 1960, Jack Kerouac retreated to a cabin here owned by Lawrence Ferlinghetti , the poet and co-founder of City Lights Bookstore. His time in the canyon formed the basis for his 1962 novel, “Big Sur.” While this is not the original Kerouac cabin, it shares the same setting.

According to Hornig, the canyon has also been home to the film director Sam Peckinpah and the Disney illustrator Ron Dias. 

“There’s an extraordinary feeling about this canyon,” Hornig says. “You’re surrounded by a landscape that inspired some of America’s most influential writers, and remarkably, much of that atmosphere of solitude and wilderness remains intact today.”

Built in 1984, the single-level home has three bedrooms, two full bathrooms, and 1,489 square feet of living space. Vaulted, open-beam ceilings, hardwood floors, and three wood-burning stoves characterize the interiors, as do large windows that frame the surrounding redwoods. A wraparound porch…
items.t: Inside a Secluded Cabin Hidden Right Beneath Big Sur’s Iconic Landmark

items.title: Inside the $7 Million Historic Georgia Estate Straight Out of ‘Practical Magic’
items.summary:
Tucked away along Pine Log Creek in Fairmount, GA , sits a nearly 71-acre historic estate that feels less like a residential listing and more like a Hollywood set. 

Known as Yarborough Mill , the $7 million property features a restored late-1800s Queen Anne Victorian—a 4,500-square-foot former grist mill and plenty of period charm. 

"It looks like something that belongs in 'Practical Magic'," says listing agent Logan Fitts with Mountain Sotheby's International Realty . “It is definitely the most historic property I've had the chance to work with, and with that it is just so unique.”

The Queen Anne Victorian is a highlight of the property. (Cheyenne Crawford) 

The property is more than 70 acres. (Cheyenne Crawford) 

The property has several structures, but the highlights are the former grist mill and a late 1800s Queen Anne Victorian.

“Everything's original, but it's all been restored because it was not in perfect condition when [the sellers] bought it. It's a complete restore project and everything is true to period,” Fitts explains. 

“The exterior of the main house, the colors she chose, the roof tiles, the architecture, and the landscaping. Everything there was intentional.”

The kitchen has been updated. (Cheyenne Crawford) 

The ceilings in many of the rooms are unique. (Cheyenne Crawford) 

The Victorian home has some Georgian features and has five bedrooms and three full bathrooms.

items.t: Inside the $7 Million Historic Georgia Estate Straight Out of ‘Practical Magic’

items.title: New Development in the Heart of Florida Equestrian Country Targets Horse Lovers With Farm Lots and Bridle Paths
items.summary:
A new masterplanned community in the heart of Palm Beach County's equestrian country has opened sales to wealthy horse lovers.

The Wellington , a private club community in the Village of Wellington , sitting about 16 miles east of West Palm Beach, will cater to the horsey set.

The 253-unit masterplanned community—with estate homes starting at $11 million and townhomes at $6.8 million—will also feature an 18-hole link-style championship golf course designed by Scottish golf course architect David McLay Kidd . The median list price in the surrounding area is $849,900, a 12% increase over last year.

But the new community will distinguish itself from the luxury development pack with high-end equestrian villas and farm lots, along with a bridle path connecting to the premiere equestrian venue, Wellington International Showgrounds.

Developer Wellington Lifestyle Partners poured capital into improving the show grounds, adding 100 acres and erecting new competition rings, a covered riding arena, a grass derby field, and stabling that's designed to prioritize ventilation, horse welfare, and rider comfort.

The improvements are expected to encourage exhibitors to arrive earlier in the fall and stay longer into the spring and summer, reinforcing the village's equestrian ecosystem, which pumps about $600 million annually into the local economy, according to the county .

The Wellington, a new gated club community, offers equestrian living in addition to a championship golf course and other amenities. (Wellington Lifestyle Partners)

items.t: New Development in the Heart of Florida Equestrian Country Targets Horse Lovers With Farm Lots and Bridle Paths

items.title: The Latest Trend in Luxury Residential Amenities? Resident-Only Salons Offering Glam on Demand
items.summary:
Luxury real estate developers are always looking for new ways to appeal to potential buyers, with resident amenities —from wellness centers to bowling alleys to sports courts —becoming commonplace. The latest offering? A private glam room.

The Greenwich, a lavish 88-story tower in New York City’s Financial District , landed on the feature as a way to give residents the ultimate luxury—a little more wiggle room in their schedule.

“From the start, we’ve looked for ways to make life easier for our residents and set The Greenwich apart from other condominium buildings,” developer Gregory Davis , Director at Fortress Investment Group, tells Realtor.com®.

“When we thought about who our residents would be and how they live, time stood out as the ultimate luxury. An in-building beauty room offering nail and hair services was a natural fit,” Davis continues.

Residents reportedly book the salon’s services weekly, with benefits ranging from quick touch-ups for meetings to full glam ahead of a gala or special occasion. The building leverages a concierge partner , LIVunLtd, to make sure scheduling is a breeze.

The Greenwich, a luxury residential tower in New York City, gives residents exclusive access to a salon and spa. (The Greenwich) 

Residents can book the space free of charge and bring their own professionals in, or can use a partner concierge service to find what they need. (The Greenwich) 

“It’s a popular and convenient amenity, particularly for those who appreciate having access to beauty and wellness services without leaving the building,” says Liz Wexler , Lifestyle…
items.t: The Latest Trend in Luxury Residential Amenities? Resident-Only Salons Offering Glam on Demand
